# FlowPilot Pitch-Deck Brief

> **FICTIONAL TEST MATERIAL**  
> FlowPilot, its customers, competitors, team members, research, financial figures, and operating results are invented solely to test presentation-generation workflows. Nothing in this document describes a real company or investment opportunity.

**Reporting date:** June 30, 2026  
**Currency:** U.S. dollars unless otherwise stated

## 1. Company Overview

FlowPilot is a fictional business-software company founded in 2023 in Denver. Its platform helps mid-sized companies automate recurring workflows across disconnected systems, coordinating steps, approvals, owners, evidence, and exceptions.

The 18-person company serves 126 paying customers as of June 30, 2026. It targets organizations that need more control than task-management software provides without the burden of enterprise automation.

## 2. Problem

Recurring work crosses CRM, accounting, HR, ticketing, and collaboration tools, while the process between them is often managed through spreadsheets, messages, and memory.

In a fictional March 2026 survey of 180 U.S. operations leaders at companies with 250–3,000 employees, 68% reported a delayed cross-functional handoff each month, 52% could not reliably prove every approval occurred, and respondents estimated a median 11 hours per week spent chasing status and evidence. These unaudited opinions may not generalize.

## 3. Solution

FlowPilot provides an orchestration layer across existing systems. Teams define workflows, owners, approvals, application connections, and exceptions without replacing their core software.

For customers launched in H1 2026, median time from contract to first live workflow was 28 days—a historical cohort result, not a guarantee. The product emphasizes fast adoption, audit history, and maintainable templates.

## 4. Target Customer

The primary customer is a North American company with 250–3,000 employees, at least five cloud systems, and a central operations, finance, IT, or customer-success team. Buyers include operations executives, chiefs of staff, controllers, and IT directors.

Priority industries are software, business services, healthcare administration, and multi-location consumer services. Customers typically begin with three workflows. Average annual contract value is $24,000.

## 5. Market Opportunity

FlowPilot’s fictional internal study estimates a $5.2 billion 2026 North American market for workflow orchestration at companies with 250–3,000 employees, excluding general project management and large-enterprise robotic automation.

Management estimates a $1.3 billion serviceable market—25% of the total—and a $130 million obtainable market, equal to 10% of serviceable and 2.5% of total. These are unaudited fictional estimates.

## 6. Product

The product combines a visual builder, conditional approvals, templates, exception queues, role-based access, audit logs, 42 packaged integrations, and an API for custom connections.

Fictional customer examples include:

- BrightPath Services reduced new-location approval time from 12 days to 7 days across 34 locations.
- Cedar Peak Software reduced median customer-onboarding time from 18 days to 13 days.
- Northline Health Administration increased completed quarterly access reviews from 81% to 96% by the deadline.

Individual results are not guaranteed outcomes.

## 7. Business Model

FlowPilot sells annual subscriptions: Growth starts at $18,000, Scale at $36,000, and Enterprise at $72,000. Pricing varies by volume, controls, and integrations. Complex migration and custom implementation cost extra.

Average contract value of $24,000 multiplied by 126 customers equals $3.024 million ARR; services are excluded.

## 8. Traction

As of June 30, 2026, FlowPilot has 126 paying customers and $3.024 million in annual recurring revenue, equivalent to $252,000 in monthly recurring revenue. Annual recurring revenue increased 80% from $1.680 million on June 30, 2025. First-half 2026 recognized revenue was $1.38 million, compared with $0.75 million in the first half of 2025, an increase of 84%.

Customer count moved from 82 on January 1, 2026 to 126 on June 30 after 52 new customers were added and eight customers churned: 82 + 52 − 8 = 126. Trailing-12-month logo retention was 92%, gross revenue retention was 90%, and net revenue retention was 116%. Gross revenue retention excludes expansion; net revenue retention includes expansion and contraction.

Qualified-trial conversion rose five percentage points, from 17% in H1 2025 to 22% in H1 2026. Median sales cycle was 47 days.

## 9. Competitive Landscape

FlowPilot competes with work-management products, enterprise automation suites, and internal tools. A fictional June 2026 review found:

| Vendor | Starting annual price | Typical deployment | Packaged integrations | Primary tradeoff |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FlowPilot | $18,000 | 28 days | 42 | Balanced control and deployment speed |
| Orchestrix | $30,000 | 60 days | 70 | Broader integration catalog, higher cost |
| TaskLane | $12,000 | 45 days | 25 | Lower entry price, lighter governance |

This directional comparison uses fictional vendor materials and 24 fictional buyer evaluations. Claims were not independently verified; prices vary.

## 10. Go-to-Market Strategy

FlowPilot combines direct sales, educational content, and referrals. Prospects enter a 21-day guided trial built around one real workflow and defined success criteria.

Planned partners include fractional operations leaders, systems integrators, and finance advisers. Management targets 26% qualified-trial conversion by June 2027, up from 22%, while keeping median sales cycle below 50 days. These are targets.

## 11. Team

Fictional CEO Maya Chen previously led mid-market operations software; CTO Daniel Ortiz built cloud-accounting integration infrastructure; Revenue VP Lena Brooks led sales to operations and finance buyers.

The 18-person team includes eight in product and engineering, four in sales and marketing, four in implementation and customer success, and two in finance and administration. Hiring priorities are engineering, security, customer success, and partnerships.

## 12. Fundraising Ask

FlowPilot is seeking a fictional **$6.0 million seed round** intended to fund approximately 24 months of operations. The proposed use of funds is:

- **45% — $2.7 million:** product and engineering, including reliability, integrations, analytics, and security;
- **30% — $1.8 million:** sales, marketing, and partner development;
- **15% — $0.9 million:** implementation and customer success; and
- **10% — $0.6 million:** compliance, finance, and general operations.

The allocations total 100% and $6.0 million. The 24-month runway is a planning estimate dependent on hiring, revenue, and expenses.

## 13. Risks

FlowPilot is early-stage. Internal market estimates may overstate demand; larger vendors can bundle workflow features; cheaper products may serve simpler use cases; and integrations depend on third-party APIs.

The company must scale implementation, maintain retention, improve security, hire effectively, and increase conversion without weakening qualification. Reported growth and retention are historical fictional results; fundraising, targets, estimates, and runway are forward-looking assumptions, not guarantees.
